Guidelines for Registration:
1. Name should be written in the application form as per name recorded in the HSLC Mark sheet / Certificate. In
   case there is discrepancy in name as recorded in HSLC documents and actual name, HSLC documents may be
   got corrected before applying for Registration with the university. In no way, the name of the candidate shall be
   modified.
2. Migration Certificate in original and downloaded from DigiLocker must be submitted in case of the students
   who have passed from Board / Council / University other than AHSEC / ASCTE. In case of on-line Migration
   Certificate, student will have to submit:
      i)       An undertaking on non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 50/- to the effect that the university issues only on
               line Migration Certificate and no Off line Migration Certificate (Hard Copy) is issued by the said
               University. Further he / she has not used / will not use this Migration Certificate for admission to
               any other university / institute simultaneously.
      ii)      On line Migration Certificate verified and certified by concerned Head of the department.
      iii)     Clause 2(i)(ii) is not applicable for those students who downloaded the Migration Certificate from
               DigiLocker.
3. While filling up the Registration form, student shall upload recent, clearly identifiable passport size photo.
   Normally no request for change of photo shall be entertained subsequently. However in exceptional cases if
   change is considered, student shall have to apply for correction/change of all the documents issued by the
   University.
4. Appropriate Gap Certificate issued by the Principal of the college / school last attended by the concerned
   student or Head of any recognized Educational Institution must be submitted in case of the students admitted
   with an intervening gap between the last examination passed / appeared and the year of admission in the present
   course.
5. No Objection Certificate (NOC) from employer shall be submitted by students who are employed in any
   Govt./Private Organisation/Institution.
6. Fees for Registration is Rs. 300/- per student and Late Fine Rs. 500/- per student to be paid On-line.

7. It is observed that in the past a good number of students submitted fake mark sheet / certificate / certificate
   from fake board / council etc. All concerned are requested to scrutinize the documents carefully and properly
   before forwarding the same to the Controller of Examination. In such cases, the admission shall be treated
   as cancelled with immediate effect. Further, appropriate action shall be initiated against such students.
8. Students will be required to apply for registration during the stipulated period, as indicated above, for the
   purpose. Failure to apply in time will lead to cancellation of admission and debarment of the concerned
   student from appearing in the semester examinations.
       i)        Student with Provisional Registration No. may appear 1st and 2nd semester examinations. Result
                 of 2nd semester examination of those students who are not formally registered with the university,
                 will not be declared/ will be kept withheld, even though Provisional Registration No. is generated
                 and received by concerned student.
       ii)       Students without formal Registration will not be allowed to appear examination from 3rd semester
                 onwards.
       iii)      In case of MPhil/PhD scholar with provisional Registration will be allowed to appear course work
                 examination, but this result will be kept withheld till formally registered with the University.
9. It should be ensured that the Registration Forms are forwarded as per intake capacity only. For any problem that
   arises due to issue of Registration Certificate more than the intake capacity, the concerned college will be
   responsible.
10. After necessary processing, Registration certificate will be issued & forwarded to the respective colleges. For
    any discrepancy in Registration Certificate(s), Principal of the concerned college may return the same in a lot
    within one month from the date of issue for necessary correction along with required documents. Application
    for correction of Registration Certificate submitted after one month must be supported by a fee of     100/- for

11. All correspondence related to students Registration should be from the Principal of the concerned college.
    Candidate should be advised not to resort to direct correspondence or persuasion for the Registration Certificate

   All concerned are requested kindly to adhere to the above strictly. Co-operation from all concerned is solicited

 History of Patharkandi College
Patharkandi College came into existence on 28th of Oct. 1990. It is situated 1. K.M away to the
east of patharkandi town. There is a big historical pond named Rajbari Pond in the east and
Patharkandi College of education (B.Ed College) in the west. The College Road runs from the
National Highway to Rajbari Pond and also a PWD road approaches to the south. The College is
surrounded by a charming place free from din and bustle environment.Though the Patharkandi
College is under the jurisdiction of L.A.2 Patharkandi constituency and H.P-I Karimganj SC Lok
Sabha (Reserved) Constituency, the huge population here are approximately 10 laks, belonging
to SC, ST, OBC, MOBC, Tea Garden General and Minority community almost 2/3 rd of whom living
Below Poverty Line. Patharkandi is one of the oldest revenue circles of the Karimganj district,
but there was no any higher educational institution in this greater area. Prof. Quomrul Hoque
was just then graduate and felt deeply the necessity of higher education at Patharkandi.

Prof. Quomrul Hoque took a bold step to start a college at patharkandi. He began to hold public meeting in different corners and getting
support from the well-wishers and wise- men and then he started degree classes at Rabindra Bhawan, Patharkandi.With a team of
enthusiastic personalities, he started tiny collection of 10 (ten) paise, 50 (fifty) paise, 1(one) Rupee etc. in order to make an awareness
                                                      and to know the people about his mission. Even paddy, betelnuts etc. were also
                                                      collected from the locality.

                                                    Prof. Quomrul Hoque also managed a plot of khas land from the district
                                                    administration at Rajbari, Patharkandi. The foundation stone of Patharkandi College
                                                    was laid down by Sri. Suresh Ch. Panda, IAS, the then Deputy Commissioner
                                                    Karimganj on the 28th oct.1990. This is the milestone of Patharkandi College. Then
                                                    the classes were shifted to Rajbari M.E. School from Rabindra Bhawan
temporarily.Construction of the College was continuing rapidly with small public collection and taking materials on credit from
merchants. Thus, a large College building was constructed.

In the meantime, Quomrul Hoque completed his Master Degree in History from Guwahati University. After which, he was appointed as a
lecturer of History at N.C. College Badarpur. Prof. Quomrul did not invest even a single penny for his future. Rather, he spent his total
amount of his salary for the construction of Patharkandi College. He himself took classes at Patharkandi College whenever he got a free
time. Gradually, the reputation of Patharkandi College started to be spread in every nook and corner of Barak Valley which is being
continued till to day.The College received its affiliation from Assam University in 1999.

Prof. Quomrul approached to DPI, Guwahati for a College affairs and while returning home, unfortunately, he died in a mysterious car
accident on 19th Oct. 1998. With the demise of Prof. Quomrul Hoque, the Patharkandi College was getting paralyzed. As a result, a few
teachers and students remained in the College. In this way, the College ran for a few years. The College rejuvenated in the year 2004
with the entrance of his younger brother, the present principal, Dr. Monjurul Hoque who then just passed out M.A. from Assam
University, Silchar. Then he rightly started to work to revive the College with an adamant mood and earned supports from teachers &
co-operation from Patharkandi College Governing Body.

He moved with his staff’s door to door to collect students and started classes regularly. Thus, the College got re -birth with its all-round
development, especially the enrolment of students, good academic atmosphere along with attractive results every year accorded in the
Assam University.However, owing to the all-round progress and prosperity, the Govt. of Assam has taken-up the College with effect from
1999.The College has already accorded permanent affiliation from the Assam University. It has 17 (Seventeen) Bighas of land o f its own.
The College has a big play ground with a tennis court. It has own library and free space of recreational facilities, canteen etc. The
College has also its own website with internet connection. All the teaching and non-teaching staffs are good and dedicating. Being a
newly provincialized College, the need of infrastructural development is very urgent. The College authority is looking forward to the kind
attention of the UGC and the relevant corners for fulfilling the dream.

Extended Centre of District Computer Centre at Patharkandi College

 The Computer Centre at Patharkandi College is an initiative aimed at empowering students
with digital skills and promoting technological literacy. This initiative is part of a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Patharkandi College and the District
Computer Training Centre, powered by AMTRON (Assam Electronics Development
Corporation Limited), Assam. The Computer Centre provides students with the opportunity to
enhance their digital skills by enrolling in various courses offered by the Centre.

Partnership with District Computer Training Centre and AMTRON: The collaboration
between Patharkandi College and the District Computer Training Centre, powered by
AMTRON, is a significant aspect of the Computer Centre initiative. AMTRON, being the state
nodal agency for implementing IT-related projects, brings valuable expertise and resources to
the partnership. This collaboration ensures that students at Patharkandi College have access to
high-quality training programs and state-of-the-art infrastructure.

Courses and Training Programs: The Computer Centre offers a wide range of courses and
training programs to cater to the diverse needs and interests of students. These programs cover
various aspects of computer education and technology, including but not limited to:

   1. Professional Diploma in Computer Application (PDCA): This course focuses on
      imparting fundamental computer skills to beginners, covering topics such as operating
      systems, file management, internet usage, and word processing.
   2. Advance Diploma in Computer Applications (ADCA): Students interested in
      programming and web development can enroll in courses that introduce them to
      programming languages, web design, and development frameworks. These courses
      enable students to create websites, web applications, and gain practical programming
      skills.
   3. Diploma in Computer Application (DCA): This course equips students with the
      knowledge and tools required for data analysis and visualization. Students learn data
      manipulation, statistical analysis, and visualization techniques using software tools
      commonly used in the industry.
   4. Post Graduate Diploma in Computer Application (PGDCSA): With the increasing
      importance of digital marketing in today's business landscape, the Computer Centre
      offers courses that cover various digital marketing strategies, including search engine
      optimization (SEO), social media marketing, content marketing, and analytics. Students
      interested in cyber security can enroll in courses that provide them with knowledge of

Bachelor in Philosophy with Honours/Honours and Research programme Objectives:
The Bachelor of Arts ( B.A.) in Philosophy with Honours and Research, offer the Four Year Under
-Graduate Programme, aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of
philosophical thought, critical reasoning, and intellectual exploration. This programme is
  designed to cultivate a deep appreciation for fundamental questions about existence, ethics,
 knowledge, and the nature of reality.
 The primarily objectives of this programme are two-fold:
 Firstly: To equip students with a strong foundation in classic and contemporary philosophical
 theories, enabling them to engage in rigorous analysis and discussion.
 Secondly: To foster advanced research skills, encouraging students to explore philosophical
 inquiries independently, contribute to existing debates, and potentially make original
 contributions to the field.
 Throughout the four -year journey, students will engage in immersive coursework, seminars,
 and debates that stimulate intellectual curiosity and analytical thinking. The programme also
 encourages students to engage with interdisciplinary perspectives, connecting philosophy with
 other fields of study. B.A. in Philosophy with Honours and Research seeks to produce graduates
 who possess a profound understanding of philosophy, advanced research capabilities, and the
 ability to apply philosophical insights to real-world context.
 PROGRAMME SPECIFIC OUTCOMES:
 1. To gain a comprehensive understanding of major philosophical theories, historical
 perspectives, and contemporary debates, enabling students to to critically analyse complex
 ideas and articulate coherent arguments.
 2. To develop the ability to independently conduct philosophical research, formulate research
 questions, gather relevant sources, and present well -structured arguments in both written and
 oral forms.
 3. To explore connections between philosophy and other disciplines, fostering a capacity to
 apply philosophical insights to broader intellectual contexts and engage in multidisciplinary
 discussions.
 4. To cultivate a heightened ethical awareness and the skills necessary to navigate complex
 moral dilemmas, enhancing students capacity for ethical decision -making in personal,
 professional, and societal contexts.
 5. To develop critical thinking skills to analyse complex issues, question assumptions, and
 evaluate diverse viewpoints. Develop effective communication skills to express philosophical
 ideas clearly and persuasively to both specialised and general audiences.

 1.1.1. The Institution ensures effective curriculum delivery through a well-planned and

documented process

Response:

Patharkandi College is an affiliated college Assam University, Silchar, and therefore follows
the syllabus and curriculum set by the university. The teachers at the college regularly
participate in departmental meetings at the university to stay updated on any revisions to the
curriculum. The university informs the college of any changes through circulars and updates
on their website. The College has made the complete syllabus and curriculum accessible on
their website for convenient access.
The college has an effective framework in place to analyse and ensure that the objectives of
the curriculum are met in letter and spirit. The college prospectus is made available at the
beginning of the academic session. All necessary information about the courses, fee structure,
faculty, etc. are made available so that students can make informed choices. The academic
processes in the college are well-organized with academic calendar, time-tables, workloads,
and administrative tasks planned ahead of time. As an affiliated college, it follows the academic
calendar provided by the university at the start of the academic year. The calendar includes a
schedule for classes, exams, breaks, and vacations that the college follows to ensure efficient
operation. The college also prepares its own calendar of events and activities (it is available on
college website). All the aforementioned information is emphasized during the orientation for
new students at the start of the academic session. Syllabus distribution among the faculty
members of the departments is done in advance before the start of the semester classes. Course
progression is recorded departmentally. The principal holds meetings with department heads,
faculty members, and all staff including non-teaching staff to ensure the smooth
implementation of the planned activities.


To ensure continuous growth, our teachers regularly enhance their knowledge through
participation in research and faculty development programs. They are also members of various
university committees, contributing to the review of curriculum, assessment, and evaluation.
To deliver the curriculum effectively, departments combine traditional classroom teaching with
various ICT tools, laboratory practical, field trips, student seminars, project works, tutorials,
and problem-solving, as required by the curriculum. The college library offers access to a large
 collection of international and national journals, reports, books, and e-resources to support the
teaching and learning processes.


Supporting the goal of effective curriculum delivery, the college implements the robust tutorial
and mentor-mentee program. Small student groups are formed for personalized academic and
other discussions. Patharkandi College places importance on combining academic and mental
well-being for our students through the mentor-mentee system, where each student is assigned
a faculty mentor for academic and personal guidance. With the focused support and guidance
from teachers, students can effectively address their academic and other concerns.
